statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-48928 is a TLS trust-policy bypass in Node.js servers with several SNI contexts: tls.Server.addContext() built a case-sensitive regular expression for the server name, so a client sending an upper-case SNI name could miss the context registered for that host and be served under the default context, whose certificate and client-certificate policy can differ. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.0, released 2026-06-18: the June 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/june-2026-security-releases, lists 22.x among the affected release lines, and the 22.23.0 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.0, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/39d1d09684 ('tls: fix case-sensitive SNI context matching'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-48928 and is in the v22.23.0 tag and not in v22.22.3; outside tests it changes lib/internal/tls/wrap.js. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-48928, lists Node.js 22 releases up to 22.22.3 as affected. The DHI nodejs-22 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-22 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-22-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-22-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-27, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 22.23.0-r0, 22.23.1-r0, 22.23.2-r0, 22.23.3-r0, 22.23.4-r0, 22.23.4-r1, 22.23.4-r2 and 22.23.5-r0 report v22.23.0 through v22.23.5 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1 and 22.22.3-r0 report v22.22.0 through v22.22.3 and are affected. As a check, the source of lib/internal/tls/wrap.js embedded in the node binary builds the addContext() server-name expression with the case-insensitive 'i' flag this fix adds in 22.23.0-r0 and every later build on both architectures, while every earlier build carries the original case-sensitive expression. 22.23.0-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
